english.title: Further disclosure of information disclosed to prosecuting authority - Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Director of Revenue and Customs Prosecutions

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), a disclosure having been made to the Director of Revenue and Customs Prosecutions in accordance with section 21 of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..), you made a further disclosure of that information which was not for a purpose connected with the exercise of the prosecuting authority's functions or with the consent of the Commissioners
english.legislation: Contrary to section 21(4) and (6) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) section 21(5) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005 provides that it is a defence for a person charged with this offence to prove that he reasonably believed
(a) that the disclosure was lawful OR
(b) that the information had already and lawfully been made available to the public.
(ii) A prosecution for this offence may be instituted only by the Director of Revenue and Customs Prosecutions or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions. Section 21(7).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 55(2) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
